opportunities.title: [Bounty $1,000] ttnn.atanh_bw returns NaN for every element whose upstream gradient is exactly zero
opportunities.summary: **Component / Area:** ttnn eltwise unary backward (composite), `atanh_bw` **Issue Type:** Bad Outputs ## Summary `atanh_bw` computes `grad / (1 - x^2)` and then applies ```cpp grad_a = where(ttnn::eqz(grad), t_nan, grad_a); // L972 grad_a = where(logical_and(eqz(grad), eqz(input)), 0.f, grad_a); // L973-978 ``` ([unary_backward.cpp#L957-L996](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/blob/9fa00fce13cda1538f0130695576408ff5b05665/ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary_backward/unary_backward.cpp#L957-L996)). The first guard was meant to encode `0 * inf = NaN` at the poles `|x| = 1`, but it has no pole condition. The second guard rescues only `x == 0`. So every position in the open interval `0 < |x| < 1`, which is the entire finite domain of `atanh`, returns NaN whenever the upstream gradient is exactly zero. Torch returns 0 there and NaN only at `|x| == 1`. Zero upstream gradients are routine (attention masks, dropout, padded positions, `where` in the graph). One zero in `grad` poisons the whole backward pass through this op. This is a source-level analysis with a host replay; I do not have a card.
